defects.claim_says: the held record contains no current-law text that names this order / no held current-law text names the Medal of Freedom order, so continuation rests on the absence of any ending event in those searches
defects.source_says: The held 5 U.S.C. 4504 note (U.S. Code release point 119-121; jobs/current-law/output/USC_EO_NOTES.jsonl and jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t5-s4504.txt, whose source record lists EO:11085) is headed 'Ex. Ord. No. 9586. The Presidential Medal of Freedom' and reads 'as amended by ... Ex. Ord. No. 11085, Feb. 22, 1963, 28 F.R. 1759; Ex. Ord. No. 11515, Mar. 13, 1970'. The claim itself mentions this 4504 note lead, so the statement is false and internally inconsistent.

defects.claim_says: The Board sections 3-6 ended 1970-03-13 when EO 11515 struck them; no current-law text is discussed
defects.source_says: The same current 5 U.S.C. 4504 note still prints sections 3 to 6 (Board, Functions of the Board, Expenses, Design) as part of the order's text, although EO 11515 sec. 5(2) struck them. The ending is correct on EO 11515's text, but the claim neither cites the current note nor explains why its editorial reprint of the struck sections does not show them continuing.

reasoning: The genuine version fixes the dates: the amendment clauses end on signing, 1963-02-22, and the Board sections end on 1970-03-13 under EO 11515 sec. 5(2). Those dates, the actors, the mechanisms, the quotes and the twelve-scope inventory are correct. No later amendment of EO 9586 after EO 11515 is held, and the YES outcome for sections 1, 2(a)-(d) and order section 2(b) is supported. Under the same standard I applied to EO 11593 and EO 10717 in the blind review, the claim still misreports the current-law record. It says no held current-law text names the order, yet the held 5 U.S.C. 4504 note prints EO 9586 as amended by EO 11085 and EO 11515, and the claim mentions that lead itself. It also leaves unaddressed that this current note reprints the struck sections 3 to 6. Rejected: correct the current-law statement, cite the note as the current predicate, and explain its reprint of the struck Board sections.
